# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I need to wait for Mute (who has the manual) and Deaf (who sees colors/markings) to share information, since the order is Mute, Blind, Deaf.

Since Mute speaks before me each round, I should wait this turn to see what Mute tells me, and gesture nothing yet since I have nothing meaningful to convey.


TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. Bomb shows: DISPLAY 3, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute, I received your gestures but I do not know their meaning yet - please have Blind confirm what he feels, and try to correlate your manual instructions to these exact colors and the display number 3.

I now know Deaf can see: DISPLAY 3, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Deaf mentioned receiving gestures from Mute already (since Mute speaks first in the order), but doesn't know their meaning. I haven't heard from Mute directly yet (Mute's speech would go to me, but I don't see anything from Mute this turn - maybe Mute only gestured, which I can't receive).

I need to relay Deaf's color/display info to Mute via speech, since Mute has the manual and needs this data to figure out instructions. I should speak to Mute with the exact details Deaf gave.

I also can report to Deaf what I physically feel about the wires (position only, no color) to help build the shared picture - though I have no distinguishing info yet since I only have positions 1-3 with no texture differences noted. I'll wait on gesturing to Deaf until I actually feel something specific.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: DISPLAY 3, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Please tell us what the manual says to do given this.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf again. Confirmed bomb state unchanged: DISPLAY 3, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute, if you want yes or no from me, use one gesture: thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no, and I will answer your yes/no questions about colors this way too. Blind, please state clearly what wire or action you intend, in speech, so I can react if I see something matching a color.

Deaf confirms the bomb state again and asks me to state clearly what action I intend, in speech, so they can react via gesture (thumbs up/down) if it matches something Deaf sees. Deaf can only see my gestures, not hear my speech — so if I speak to Mute, Deaf won't get it. I need to gesture my intent to Deaf directly, not speak it, since Deaf cannot hear.

I still haven't heard anything from Mute (who has the manual). Mute speaks first each round; maybe Mute has only gestured so far, which reaches Deaf and me both, but I don't receive gestures at all — so I wouldn't know if Mute gestured anything. I need Mute to actually speak to me so I get instructions.

I should proceed carefully: I have no manual instruction yet on what to actually cut. I don't want to act blindly. Let me push Mute for actual spoken instructions, and use gesture to Deaf to establish a simple protocol (e.g., I can gesture wire numbers via finger counts to see if Deaf can confirm anything against the manual's color mapping once Mute deciphers it).

For now, I have not been told which wire to cut. I will not act. I'll speak to Mute asking for explicit instructions, and gesture to Deaf indicating I have received their message (a simple acknowledgment) without committing to any wire yet.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I have not heard any spoken instructions from you yet. Please tell me in speech which wire to cut, or what action to take, based on Deaf's colors: DISPLAY 3, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤙"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf: bomb unchanged, DISPLAY 3, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. I saw gesture wire-1 thumbs-up from Mute, and a signal from Blind. Mute, please confirm: is wire 1 the one to cut? Use gesture one-finger plus thumbs-up for yes, one-finger plus thumbs-down for no. Blind, please describe in speech what you feel on the bomb so Mute and I can match it to what I see.

Progress! Deaf saw a gesture from Mute suggesting "wire-1 thumbs-up" — meaning Mute may be indicating wire 1 is the one to cut, based on the manual. Deaf is asking Mute to confirm via gesture, and asking me to describe what I feel so we can cross-check.

I should describe my physical/tactile findings on the bomb to help confirm. Since I don't have any texture info yet in my view (the ACTION BOARD still shows [?] for everything), let me report what I actually feel - though the board hasn't given me any tactile detail. I should state plainly what I can act on: I can cut wire 1, 2, or 3, but I have no sensory distinguishing information from touch alone (no texture noted). I'll convey this limitation, and wait for Mute's explicit confirmation before cutting anything, since a wrong cut kills us all.

I'll speak to Mute asking for direct spoken confirmation, since gestures between Mute and Deaf don't reach me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I feel three wires at positions 1, 2, and 3, but no distinguishing texture or marking reaches me by touch alone. I need your explicit spoken confirmation: should I cut wire 1? Please say yes or no in words.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf here. Bomb shows DISPLAY 3, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute has signaled twice, wire one thumbs up, meaning wire 1 the red wire is the one to cut. Please confirm with Mute via speech before you act, since I cannot hear your exchange.

Deaf is now relaying to me directly (since Deaf can see Mute's gestures) that Mute signaled "wire 1 thumbs up" twice, meaning wire 1 (the red wire) is the one to cut. But this comes secondhand through Deaf's interpretation of a gesture, not directly from Mute in speech to me. I still haven't received any actual speech from Mute confirming this.

Given the stakes, I should get direct spoken confirmation from Mute before acting. Let me ask Mute one more explicit time, referencing what Deaf relayed, to get a direct "yes" in words from Mute since that's the only channel Mute has to reach me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf tells me you gestured wire 1 thumbs-up, meaning cut wire 1 the red wire. Please confirm in speech: yes, cut wire 1? I will act only after you confirm in words.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf: final confirmation, Mute has signaled wire one thumbs-up three times consistently. Bomb still shows DISPLAY 3, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. I believe wire 1, the red wire, is safe to cut. Proceed if Mute's manual agrees.

Mute has consistently gestured "wire 1 thumbs-up" three times now, confirmed by Deaf, indicating the manual says to cut wire 1. However, I still have never received a direct spoken word from Mute — Mute may only be able to gesture in this scenario, or perhaps Mute's speech to me isn't arriving for some reason. Given the consistency of three independent confirmations from Deaf about Mute's gesture, and the risk of continuing to stall indefinitely, this is a strong enough signal to act.

The rules state Mute cannot speak — wait, checking the role table: "Mute: Can read manual; Cannot speak, or touch bomb." So Mute cannot speak at all! That's why I've never received speech from Mute — Mute literally cannot speak. My repeated requests for "spoken confirmation" were impossible to fulfill. Mute can only gesture, which only Deaf (and Mute reflexively) can see, not me. So Deaf relaying Mute's gestures via speech to me is actually the only pathway for Mute's information to reach me.

Given that, three consistent confirmations relayed by Deaf about Mute's gesture (wire 1, thumbs-up) is the best and only evidence I will ever get. I should proceed.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
